editorial.description_en: Dry sand above the tideline — the first colour in this group warm enough to be called sand rather than off-white.
editorial.description_ja: 乾いた砂のような、あたたかみのある明るい色。

provenance.derivation: Editorial construction, not a measurement. Specified in OKLCh as L 0.862, C 0.024, h 80.0° and converted to canonical D65 XYZ by @irodora/color-spaces 0.1.0 (oklchToXyz), rounded to six decimal places. Re-derivable from this sentence alone.
provenance.editorialNotes: Name coined by Irodora: 乾き (kawaki, dryness) + 砂 (suna, sand). It is not asserted to be a traditional Japanese colour name, and the hyphenated romaji marks it as a constructed compound (ADR-0065). "Dry Sand" is an editorial decision about what communicates in English, not a literal translation of 乾砂. Relations asserted from measured proximity under the current engine, not from a source: related is the three nearest in CIELAB — furu-gami at ΔE00 2.7, shira-tsuchi at ΔE00 3.1, haru-moya at ΔE00 3.6. complementary is empty because at chroma 0.024 the hue is not a reliable enough statement to oppose. historicalVariants is empty: this entry makes no historical claim to vary from.
